description:
The Dairy Farming Scheme under the Haryana State Cooperative Dairy Federation Limited (HSFDC) was launched in 2016. 

This scheme aims to promote dairy farming as a sustainable livelihood option for rural households in Haryana. 

The primary objective of the Dairy Farming Scheme is to enhance milk production in the state. 

The scheme also aims to improve the income of dairy farmers by providing them with financial assistance and necessary resources. 

The target is to increase the milk production in Haryana from 7.5 million liters per day to 10 million liters per day by the year 2025. 

The scheme focuses on providing assistance to small and marginal farmers. 

It also aims to empower women by encouraging their participation in dairy farming. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided for the purchase of high-yielding dairy animals. 

Farmers can receive up to ₹30,000 for the purchase of a high-yielding cow. 

For buffaloes, the assistance amount is up to ₹40,000. 

The scheme also provides support for the construction of dairy sheds. 

Farmers can receive up to ₹25,000 for building a dairy shed. 

The Dairy Farming Scheme includes training programs for farmers. 

These programs cover various aspects of dairy farming, including animal husbandry and veterinary care. 

The training is conducted by the Haryana Dairy Development Department. 

Eligibility for the Dairy Farming Scheme includes being a resident of Haryana. 

Applicants must be small or marginal farmers. 

The age limit for applicants is between 18 to 60 years. 

Income criteria require that the annual income of the applicant should not exceed ₹1.5 lakh. 

Educational qualifications are not strictly defined but a basic understanding of dairy farming is preferred. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested farmers must obtain the application form from the nearest HSFDC office. 

The application form can also be downloaded from the official HSFDC website. 

Farmers must fill out the application form with accurate details. 

Required documents include proof of residence, income certificate, and identity proof. 

Farmers must also provide details of the land owned. 

Once the application is completed, it should be submitted to the nearest HSFDC office. 

The application will be reviewed by the officials. 

After verification, eligible applicants will receive financial assistance. 

The disbursement of funds is typically made within 30 days of approval. 

The scheme operates on a continuous basis. 

There are no specific deadlines for applications. 

However, farmers are encouraged to apply as soon as possible to avail of the benefits. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Haryana State Cooperative Dairy Federation Limited. 

The contact details for HSFDC can be found on their official website. 

Farmers can also reach out to the Haryana Dairy Development Department for assistance. 

The Dairy Farming Scheme has been instrumental in increasing the number of dairy farmers in Haryana. 

As of 2023, the scheme has supported over 10,000 farmers across the state. 

The average increase in milk production per farmer has been reported at 15 liters per day. 

The scheme has also contributed to the establishment of cooperative dairy societies. 

These societies help in the collective marketing of milk and dairy products. 

The government has allocated ₹50 crores for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2023-2024. 

The Dairy Farming Scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries. 

Many farmers have reported improved livelihoods and better quality of life. 

The scheme also promotes the use of modern technology in dairy farming. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt practices such as artificial insemination and proper feeding techniques. 

The government conducts regular workshops to educate farmers on these practices. 

The Dairy Farming Scheme is part of a broader initiative to boost the agricultural sector in Haryana. 

It aligns with the national goal of increasing milk production in India. 

The scheme is expected to play a crucial role in achieving self-sufficiency in milk production. 

The government aims to increase the contribution of the dairy sector to the state's GDP. 

The Dairy Farming Scheme also emphasizes the importance of animal welfare. 

Farmers are trained on proper care and management of dairy animals. 

The scheme has provisions for veterinary services and health check-ups for the animals. 

The government collaborates with various NGOs for the effective implementation of the scheme. 

These NGOs assist in outreach and awareness programs for potential beneficiaries. 

The Dairy Farming Scheme is a significant step towards rural development in Haryana. 

It not only supports farmers economically but also contributes to food security. 

The scheme has the potential to transform the dairy landscape in the state. 

It encourages sustainable farming practices that benefit both farmers and the environment. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the scheme for improvements. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account for future enhancements. 

The Dairy Farming Scheme represents a commitment to empowering rural communities. 

It aims to create a self-reliant and prosperous dairy farming sector in Haryana. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's efforts in promoting agriculture and allied sectors. 

Overall, the Dairy Farming Scheme under HSFDC is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses multiple facets of dairy farming from financial assistance to training and support. 

Farmers are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme for better livelihoods. 

The scheme exemplifies the government's focus on rural development and agricultural sustainability.
